g.text: In a traditional design, performing the same instruction on three data points
(D1...D3) requires the instruction to be read three times (I1...I3).
Performance is improved in MIMD machines by distributing the operations across
multiple processors, but this still requires the instruction to read three times and
A SIMD design simplifies the MIMD design by using a single CPU and reading a
single instruction. This is less expensive because only the FPU circuitry is
duplicated, but the downside is the instructions have to be the same for every data
point. This is common, and useful, in multimedia data.
